recipes.name: Banana Trifle
ingredients_raw: 2 (3.5 ounce) packages instant banana pudding mix
1 (12 ounce) package prepared pound cake, cubed
0.5 (12 ounce) box vanilla wafers (such as Nilla®), crushed

steps.text: Whisk milk and pudding mix together in a bowl until smooth; stir in chopped bananas. Set aside.

Beat cream in a large chilled glass or metal bowl until stiff peaks are just about to form. Beat in sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form, making sure not to overbeat, or whipped cream will become lumpy and butter-like.

Layer 1/2 each pound cake cubes, pudding, whipped cream, and crushed vanilla wafers in a trifle bowl. Repeat layering with remaining 1/2 each cake, pudding, and whipped cream; top with remaining 1/2 crushed vanilla wafers. Refrigerate until chilled and ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Trifle
raw_recipe.description: This banana trifle recipe layers pound cake, whipped cream, banana pudding, and vanilla wafer cookies to form this easy trifle that's sure to please.

review.reviewBody: MARVELOUS! I made this recipe exactly as stated. It gave such a nice presentation. I crushed the vanilla wafers by putting them in a zip lock bag and using a rolling pin. When I dished the dessert out, I sprinkled the top with extra crushed vanilla wafers I had set aside. It was the hit of the night. Thank you CNM CATERING for such an awesome recipe!

Was a great recipie! I made my own pudding though instead of using the packages of instant! I put the whip cream into a big ziploc and snipped the end of it and pipped it into the trifle, so I would get the perfect layers from the outside! It was the best looking trifle I've made yet! yum!

I have been making this for years. It is a family favorite. I add layer of sliced strawberries before each layer of banana's for a bit more flavor. I use yellow cake if I don't have pound cake, it works fine. Sometimes I will spread strawberry jelly on the cake before I slice it up for more flavor. Trifle looks fancy, but is a simple way to use up a lot of odds and ends in your kitchen.

I made this for a group of my friends and I made a few changes and everyone thought my girlfriend made it..I added banana liquor to the pound cake. I then did 1 layer with cream cheese pudding and 1 layer with French Vanilla pudding .. it was so decadent.

I made this but used store bought pound cake to save time and added crushed health bars along with the crushed vanilla wafers which i did with a zip lock bag and rolling pin. It was delicious and the homemade whipped cream versus using cool whip or redi whip made it even better and was easy to do. Looks fancy but not hard to make. Got many compliments and will definitely make again.

Holy cow! This was amazing! I made it for the first time today and brought it to work. It was a big hit. So simple to make. I used angel food cake instead of pound cake because that's what I had on hand. Next time I'll probably whip the cream longer to thicken it up more, but the taste can't be beat. Very nice trifle :)

I quadrupled the recipe for a church dinner, and I thought it tasted good, but I would recommend using vanilla pudding mix instead of banana flavor, which to me has an odd taste. I used Cool Whip instead of real whipped cream, and I did not use the vanilla wafers. It was an easy dessert to serve to a crowd, and I liked the pound cake as a base. I added caramel sauce to the layers of pound cake and drizzled it on top.

I love to make trifles to take to get togethers, because their presentation is so fun! Everyone will try it, because their so pretty! Well, this was the hit of the UFC fight party!! Most everyone went back for seconds! I followed the directions exactly, except for the pound cake. I purchased a cinnamon sugar loaf from Costco from their bakery (in a pack of 3, so I can make this two more time!). The cinnamon made it especially yummy! Oh, and I used 3 bananas instead of 2, and it wasn't too much. Definitely one of my favorite trifles ever!!

Made this for an Easter dessert for a family gathering of 24. I used two small boxes of sugar-free vanilla pudding (I went by serving size, not by weight), and I used 3 sliced bananas due to the size of my trifle bowl. I used "bite sized" store-brand vanilla wafers, and they weren't much smaller than normal size. The only thing I would change is to add a note to "trim off all brown sides of the pound cake before cutting into cubes," becuase in my opinion, I prefer to see the brown vanilla wafers, and I prefer the pound cake to be a nice yellow color, but I'm my own worst critic, and nobody complained. This was very well-received, and it's on my "keeper" list for potlucks. Next time I'll make my own pound cake a day or two in advance, since the saralee brand contains high fructose corn syrup, which isn't good for anyone. Thanks to CNM for a wonderful presentation!

Outstanding! Made for a holiday open house and those who like banana LOVED this. Four cups of cream was way too much for my standard-sized trifle bowl though; next time I will use three cups with about a 1/2 cup of sugar. Also, I'll put most of the vanilla wafers on the first layer; I had too much left over after covering the top.
You can put lemon juice with the sliced bananas before layering it to keep the bananas from turning brown.
I would just buy whipped cream, making it made a complete mess but, I'm happy I had this experience! 😊
Great recipe! I used vanilla cream oreos instead of vanilla wafers. And, cool whip instead of homemade cream. It's a keeper!!
It was so good, I made it for Christmas. Didn't make any changes it was a big hit!!!
I followed the recipe and it turned out beautifully! So many compliments! Everyone loved it. It was light and not overly sweet. Make it!
This was easy and fun to make...definitely a crowd pleaser! The only thing I added was homemade strawberry compote on top of the whipped cream layer to give it a sweet boost!
This was super easy to make and it was fantastic! Great dessert after dinner, and even better as leftovers for breakfast the next morning.

I made this trifle for Memorial Day and followed the recipe to a T. My family raved about how good it was and I loved it! It is a perfect Summer dessert but as far as I'm concerned, I could eat this trifle any old day. It's rich, but not overly rich. The banana taste is very prominent, as it should be, but the whipped cream amd crushed wafer crumbs create a dreamy balance! 
This was my first attempt at making a trifle, and I was very pleased with the end result. Because of this recipe, I'm definitely making more trifles in the future! 5/5!
Highly recommend this recipe to anyone who is a banana lover. It is easy to make and so simple to put together. So tasty it will be gone by the end of the day!
Made it as the recipe dictated. The perfect light desert after a meal. I'll make it again!
